cases.case_name: ARSHAD NEYAZ KHAN v. STATE OF JHARKHAND & ANOTHER
cases.abstract_facts: The appellant, the owner of certain properties, entered into an agreement to sell these properties to the complainant in 2013, receiving an advance payment. The appellant failed to transfer the property or return the advance, leading to a complaint in 2021 alleging cheating, breach of trust, and conspiracy. The appellant sought anticipatory bail, which was initially granted but later canceled due to non-compliance with conditions. The High Court refused to quash the proceedings but allowed the appellant to apply for bail again. The appellant appealed to the Supreme Court.
cases.disposition: The appeal is allowed, and the proceedings and FIR quashed.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail cancelled; proceedings not quashed but allowed to reapply for bail.

cases.case_name: Nikita Jagganath Shetty @ Nikita Vishwajeet Jadhav v. State of Maharashtra & Anr.
cases.petitioner: Nikita Jagganath Shetty @ Nikita Vishwajeet Jadhav
cases.respondent: The State of Maharashtra and Another
cases.abstract_facts: The case involves a criminal appeal against the grant of anticipatory bail by the High Court to several accused involved in a property dispute. The complainant alleges that her estranged husband and co-accused attempted to forcibly take possession of a property, a hotel, that she inherited. The appellant seeks cancellation of anticipatory bail due to the accused's criminal actions, including trespass and threatening behavior.
cases.disposition: The Supreme Court quashed the High Court's order granting anticipatory bail and directed the accused to surrender.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail granted by the High Court.

cases.case_name: Dukhishyam Benupani v. Arun Kumar Bajoria
cases.petitioner: DUKHISHYAM BENUPANI, ASSTT. DIRECTOR, ENFORCEMENT DIRECTORATE (FERA)
cases.abstract_facts: The case involves allegations against the respondent concerning violations of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA). The Enforcement Directorate sought to interrogate the respondent regarding documents and materials obtained during a raid. The respondent was granted anticipatory bail by the City Sessions Court, a decision challenged by the Directorate. The Calcutta High Court added further restrictions on arresting the respondent, leading to the appeal in the Supreme Court.
cases.disposition: Anticipatory bail and High Court order set aside, allowing the appeal.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail granted to the respondent, with conditions for reporting.

cases.case_name: K. BASA V ARATAPP A v. TAX RECOVERY COMMISSIONER, BANGALORE AND OTHERS
cases.abstract_facts: The appellant entered into an agreement with a property owner, who had defaulted in income tax payments, to purchase certain properties. The tax authorities attached and auctioned the properties to recover tax dues. The appellant moved to set aside the auction, claiming locus through a pending specific performance suit. The High Court initially allowed his application, but a Division Bench later reversed it. The appellant appealed to the Supreme Court.
cases.disposition: The appeal was dismissed, upholding the High Court Division Bench's decision.
cases.lower_court_outcome: The High Court Division Bench ruled against the appellant, dismissing his application to set aside the auction sale.

cases.case_name: Nirmal Jeet Kaur v. State of Madhya Pradesh
cases.respondent: The State of Madhya Pradesh and Anr.
cases.abstract_facts: A woman lodged a complaint against her husband alleging physical and mental torture due to dowry demands. Offences under IPC Sections 498A, 506/34 and the Dowry Prohibition Act were alleged. The husband sought protection under Section 438 CrPC, which was granted temporarily, and later applied for regular bail under Section 439 CrPC, which was contested leading to this Supreme Court appeal.
cases.disposition: Appeal allowed; High Court order granting protection to Respondent No. 2 under Section 438 CrPC unsustainable.
cases.lower_court_outcome: High Court granted temporary protection under Section 438 CrPC, directing a later bail application under Section 439 CrPC.

cases.case_name: POKAR RAM v. STATE OF RAJASTHAN AND ANR
cases.abstract_facts: This case involves an incident where an individual was injured and later died due to firearm injuries. The police registered an initial case for attempted murder, which was later escalated to murder after the victim's death. The accused sought anticipatory bail, which was granted by the Sessions Judge despite objections. The appellant sought to cancel the bail, citing procedural deviations and misuse of judicial discretion.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail granted

cases.case_name: SALAUDDIN ABDULSAMAD SHAIKH v. THE STATE OF MAHARASHTRA
cases.abstract_facts: The case involves a petitioner who applied for anticipatory bail under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, due to fear of arrest in a non-bailable crime. The High Court initially granted an ad-interim anticipatory bail with conditions, which was to last until a specified date. Upon its expiry, the High Court directed the petitioner to apply for regular bail before the appropriate court. The decision was contested, leading to the special leave petition in the Supreme Court of India.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Ad-interim anticipatory bail granted with conditions

cases.case_name: Sunita Devi v. State of Bihar and Ors.
cases.abstract_facts: The informant lodged a complaint alleging that the respondent, armed with weapons and a revolver, demanded money from her brother and attempted to commit a crime against the informant. An FIR was lodged, and the respondent sought anticipatory bail under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, which the High Court granted unconditionally. The Supreme Court reviewed the blanket bail protection given by the High Court, finding it contrary to the procedural requirements.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail granted by the High Court

cases.case_name: Balchand Jain v. State of Madhya Pradesh
cases.abstract_facts: A Food Inspector raided the shop of the appellant, a merchant dealing in kiryana goods and kerosene oil, seizing his account books. Fearing arrest for a non-bailable offence under the Defence and Internal Security of India Act and Rules, the appellant sought anticipatory bail under Section 438 of CrPC. Both the Sessions Court and the High Court rejected his application, the latter ruling that Rule 184 of the Defence and Internal Security of India Rules superseded Section 438.
cases.disposition: Appeal allowed and remanded to High Court for reconsideration on merits.
normalized_statutes: Defence and Internal Security of India Rules, 1971:184
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail denied by Sessions Court and High Court relying on Rule 184.

cases.case_name: NIRANJAN SINGH & ANR. v. PRABHAKAR RAJARAM KHAROTE & ORS.
cases.abstract_facts: The case involves two sub-inspectors and eight police constables accused of conspiring to murder the brother of the complainant. It is alleged that the police dragged the victim out of a truck, tied him to a tree, and shot him. While the lower courts had granted bail, the complainant argued that the accused, not being in custody, were abusing their freedom by threatening him. The Supreme Court considered the points on custody, bail, and the responsibilities of the state in handling such serious charges against police officers.
cases.disposition: Supreme Court did not interfere with the bail decision but emphasized supervisory requirements for police officers on bail.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Bail granted by the Sessions Court, with conditions added by the High Court.

cases.case_name: GURBAKSH SINGH SIBBIA ETC. v. STATE OF PUNJAB
cases.abstract_facts: The case involves allegations against a former Minister of Irrigation and Power in the Punjab government, accused of political corruption. Anticipatory bail applications were filed in the High Court, which were then referred to a Full Bench. The High Court imposed several constraints on the grant of anticipatory bail, emphasizing it should be rarely used. The appeals reached the Supreme Court to address the balance between individual liberty and investigational powers of the police under Section 438 of CrPC 1973.
cases.lower_court_outcome: The Full Bench of the High Court dismissed the anticipatory bail applications, outlining strict limitations for granting such bail.

cases.case_name: Adri Dharan Das v. State of West Bengal
cases.abstract_facts: A complaint was filed alleging various offences under Sections 406, 467, 468, 471, and 420 IPC against the appellant and five others. It was alleged that the appellant, a former president of a temple, and others committed the offences. An application for anticipatory bail was filed under Section 438 CrPC, which the Calcutta High Court rejected, leading to the present appeal.
cases.disposition: Appeal disposed of; no anticipatory bail granted
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail application rejected by Calcutta High Court

cases.case_name: Naresh Kumar Yadav v. Ravindra Kumar
cases.abstract_facts: The informant challenged the High Court's order granting anticipatory bail to three respondents under Section 438 of the CrPC. The informant contended that the High Court erroneously noted the accused were not named in the FIR and pre-empted charge framing. The Supreme Court considered the legal principles of anticipatory bail and the correct procedures for granting it under Sections 438 and 439 of the CrPC.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail granted under Section 438 of the CrPC.

cases.case_name: Savitri Agarwal v. State of Maharashtra
cases.abstract_facts: The appellants, who are family members of the deceased, were accused of dowry death and cruelty after the deceased, Laxmi, died from burn injuries. Despite Laxmi's initial accidental explanation in her dying declarations, their anticipatory bail granted by the Sessions Judge was revoked by the High Court due to neglected incriminating circumstances. The Supreme Court was approached to contest this revocation.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail granted by Sessions Judge but later canceled by the High Court.

cases.case_name: Ravindra Saxena v. State of Rajasthan
cases.abstract_facts: The appellant applied for anticipatory bail which was rejected for the third time by the High Court of Rajasthan, Jaipur Bench. The case arose from a complaint by the complainant who alleged that the appellant, along with others, accepted the necessary consideration for two flats but sold them to another party, constituting alleged offences under various sections of the IPC. The appellant claimed abuse of the criminal process by the investigating officer, related civil litigation pressure, and prior unsuccessful bail applications. The Supreme Court assessed the legality of anticipatory bail rejection.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Bail application rejected by High Court

cases.case_name: HDFC Bank Ltd. v. J.J. Mannan
cases.respondent: J.J. Mannan @ J.M. John Paul & Anr.
cases.abstract_facts: The appellant, a bank, extended a loan for purchasing machinery. It was later discovered that the loan amount was not used for the intended purpose, and the beneficiary was accused of colluding with accomplices to defraud the bank. An FIR was filed alleging offences under multiple IPC sections. The respondent obtained anticipatory bail, which was interpreted to preclude any appearance or surrender during the investigation and trial. The Supreme Court modified the anticipatory bail order, emphasizing the requirement for regular bail after charges.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail granted to respondent by High Court

cases.case_name: Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra
cases.abstract_facts: The case involves a member of a political party who, along with his brother, allegedly instigated their party workers to fire gunshots at workers of a rival political party, leading to the murder of one person. The murder occurred eight days after the alleged instigation. The High Court rejected an anticipatory bail application by the accused, resulting in this appeal to the Supreme Court.
cases.disposition: Appeal allowed. Anticipatory bail granted with conditions.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail application rejected by the High Court.

cases.case_name: BHASKAR MISHRA v. STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH
cases.abstract_facts: The petitioner was charged under Section 307 of the IPC in Madhya Pradesh. He filed multiple bail applications, attempting to secure anticipatory and regular bail. After being granted anticipatory bail for a limited period, he failed to appear in subsequent hearings, citing illness. His repeated bail requests were dismissed by the Sessions and High Court, as well as a Special Leave Petition to the Supreme Court, citing misuse of the judicial process.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Dismissed applications for bail due to absconding.

cases.case_name: JAi PRAKASH SINGH v. THE STATE OF BIHAR & ANR. ETC.
cases.respondent: THE STATE OF BIHAR & ANR. ETC.
cases.abstract_facts: In this case, a FIR was lodged by the appellant against two respondents under Sections 302/34 IPC for the alleged murder of his brother. The incident allegedly occurred after a long-standing account dispute. The respondents were granted anticipatory bail by the Patna High Court, which was challenged by the appellant. The Supreme Court deliberated on the correctness of the anticipatory bail granted based on the gravity of the offense and compliance with statutory provisions.
cases.disposition: The anticipatory bail granted by the High Court was set aside by the Supreme Court.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail granted to respondents by the High Court.

cases.case_name: Rashmi Rekha Thatoi v. State of Orissa
cases.abstract_facts: The case involves the legality of orders issued by the High Court of Orissa regarding anticipatory bail applications. Although the High Court expressed reluctance to grant anticipatory bail, it directed the release of some accused upon surrendering on such terms as deemed fit by the Magistrate. The Supreme Court reviewed these directions from the High Court, as the orders issued could create legal uncertainties and potentially violate statutory provisions.
cases.lower_court_outcome: The High Court directed that some accused would be released on bail upon surrender to the Magistrate, despite not granting anticipatory bail.

cases.case_name: LAVE SH v. STATE (NCT OF DELHI)
cases.abstract_facts: An FIR was registered alleging that the appellant's younger brother's wife committed suicide in her matrimonial home, having been subjected to cruelty by her in-laws for dowry demands. The appellant, along with other family members, faced charges following the suicide. The Sessions Court and the High Court both rejected the appellant's applications for anticipatory bail, leading to an appeal in the Supreme Court.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail application rejected by Sessions Court and High Court.

cases.case_name: Vilas Pandurang Pawar & Anr. v. State of Maharashtra & Ors.
cases.abstract_facts: The case involves a dispute over rainwater between neighbors where the complainant alleges that the accused abused and assaulted the complainant and their family by referring to their caste. An FIR was filed under various IPC sections and Section 3(1)(x) of the SC/ST Act. The accused sought anticipatory bail, but the session and high courts rejected their application, leading to a special leave petition to the Supreme Court.
normalized_statutes: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989:18
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail rejected by Sessions Court and partly by High Court.

cases.case_name: Sumit Mehta v. State of N.C.T. of Delhi
cases.abstract_facts: The petitioner was granted anticipatory bail by the High Court with a condition to deposit Rs. 1 crore in a fixed deposit in the name of the complainant. The petitioner challenged this condition, arguing it was outside the scope of Section 438 of the CrPC and contrary to Article 21 of the Constitution of India. The Supreme Court examined whether such a condition for bail was legally sustainable and decided the condition was onerous and unreasonable, thus setting it aside, but retained other conditions for the anticipatory bail.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail granted with condition to deposit money.

cases.case_name: State of Madhya Pradesh v. Pradeep Sharma
cases.abstract_facts: The case involves a murder where the victim was allegedly poisoned due to an enmity related to a local election. The respondent was accused of conspiring with others to poison the victim by offering him a drink with poison. The High Court granted anticipatory bail to the accused despite being absconders, which was later challenged in the Supreme Court.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail granted

cases.case_name: Km. Hema Mishra v. State of U.P.
cases.abstract_facts: An FIR was lodged against the petitioner alleging fraud and forgery concerning the preparation of documents for appointment as an Assistant Teacher. The petitioner sought to quash the FIR and obtain pre-arrest bail through a writ petition under Article 226, after Section 438 CrPC was omitted in Uttar Pradesh. The High Court dismissed the writ petition, leading to this appeal on the jurisdiction to grant pre-arrest protection under extraordinary circumstances.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Writ petition dismissed by High Court; interim relief declined

cases.case_name: Sundeep Kumar Bafna v. State of Maharashtra
cases.abstract_facts: The petitioner sought regular bail from the High Court under Section 439 of the CrPC after being denied anticipatory bail. The High Court dismissed the application, claiming it lacked jurisdiction since the magistrate's custody was necessary. The petitioner was facing charges under multiple sections of the IPC and his case had been committed to the Sessions Court. The Supreme Court reviewed whether the High Court had jurisdiction in matters of bail when the accused surrenders.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Bail application dismissed by the Bombay High Court

cases.case_name: Bhadresh Bipinbhai Sheth v. State of Gujarat
cases.abstract_facts: The appellant was initially charged in 2001 under Section 506(2) of the IPC for criminal intimidation. Allegations of rape were not included until 2014 when a new charge under Section 376 IPC was added. The appellant was initially granted anticipatory bail by the Sessions Judge, which was later canceled by the High Court. The Supreme Court addressed whether the addition of a rape charge after a significant delay justified denying anticipatory bail, considering the appellant participated in court proceedings without attempting to flee the course of justice.
cases.disposition: Anticipatory bail granted by sessions court restored
cases.lower_court_outcome: Cancellation of anticipatory bail

cases.case_name: Sudhir v. State of Maharashtra
cases.abstract_facts: Two engineers from the Rural Water Supply Department were accused of misappropriating public funds meant for rural development, specifically relating to the construction of water facilities and public toilets in villages. Initial anticipatory bail was granted by a Sessions Judge but later cancelled by the High Court due to the serious nature of the allegations and the need for custodial interrogation.
cases.disposition: The Supreme Court upheld the High Court's decision to cancel anticipatory bail.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail granted by the Additional Sessions Judge.

cases.case_name: Prem Giri (S) v. State of Rajasthan (S)
cases.abstract_facts: The appellant, apprehending arrest for offences under various IPC sections due to an FIR filed at Police Station Jaitaran, sought anticipatory bail under Section 438 of the CrPC. The High Court dismissed the application without assigning reasons, leading to the appeal in the Supreme Court.
cases.disposition: Appeal allowed; matter remanded to High Court for fresh decision.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Bail application rejected by High Court without reasons.

cases.case_name: Manju Devi v. Onkarjit Singh Ahluwalia
cases.respondent: ONKARJIT SINGH AHLUWALIA @ OMKARJEET SINGH & OTHERS
cases.abstract_facts: The case involves allegations by a woman belonging to a Scheduled Caste that the accused entered her quarters to outrage her modesty, insulted her using offensive caste-related terms, and threatened her for revealing the incident. The complaint was initially reported to the police leading to an FIR, and later a magisterial cognizance was taken despite a police closure report. The accused sought anticipatory bail, which was granted by the High Court, leading to an appeal by the complainant to the Supreme Court.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail granted

cases.case_name: Satpal Singh v. State of Punjab
cases.abstract_facts: The appellant sought anticipatory bail in an FIR filed under sections 22 and 29 of the NDPS Act. The application was filed on the grounds of parity since two co-accused had been granted anticipatory bail by a coordinate Bench of the High Court. However, the High Court rejected the bail due to limitations under section 37 of the NDPS Act. The Sessions Court incorrectly granted regular bail to the accused based on an interim order. The Supreme Court held that the High Court's rejection of anticipatory bail was correct under section 37.
cases.disposition: Appeal by accused dismissed. Appeal by State allowed.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail denied by High Court.

cases.case_name: Dr. Subhash Kashinath Mahajan v. State of Maharashtra
cases.respondent: The State of Maharashtra and Anr.
cases.abstract_facts: In 2006, a government employee belonging to a Scheduled Caste lodged an FIR against two senior officers for making an adverse entry in his Annual Confidential Report. The appellant, Dr. Subhash Kashinath Mahajan, refused in 2011 to sanction proceedings against the officers. In 2016, a new FIR was lodged against the appellant, leading him to seek quashing of proceedings. The High Court rejected the quashing request, prompting the appeal.
cases.disposition: The appeal was allowed, and the proceedings against the appellant were quashed.
normalized_statutes: The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989:18
cases.lower_court_outcome: Request for quashing of proceedings was rejected by the High Court.

cases.case_name: P. CHIDAMBARAM v. DIRECTORATE OF ENFORCEMENT
cases.abstract_facts: The case involves allegations of irregularities in Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) clearance given to INX Media for receiving foreign investments significantly exceeding approved inflow. The former finance minister and others faced charges, including conspiracy and money laundering. The Supreme Court was called to decide on anticipatory bail, previously denied by the Delhi High Court, in a case involving significant financial discrepancies, influence peddling, and subsequent money laundering investigations.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Application for anticipatory bail was dismissed by the High Court.

cases.case_name: P. SURENDRAN v. STATE BY INSPECTOR OF POLICE
cases.abstract_facts: The petitioner filed for anticipatory bail in a case involving allegations under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. The District Judge initially denied bail, and the High Court Registry refused to number and list the application over maintainability concerns, as the offence was under the SC/ST Act. The Supreme Court examined whether the Registry's refusal impinged on the judicial function of the High Court.
cases.disposition: Petition disposed of; High Court Registry directed to number and list the application.
normalized_statutes: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989:3(II)
Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989:18A
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail denied by District Judge; High Court Registry refused to number the application.

cases.case_name: Sumedh Singh Saini v. State of Punjab
cases.abstract_facts: An FIR was lodged against the appellant for alleged offences that took place in 1991, initially for crimes under various sections of IPC, and later adding Section 302 based on co-accused statements. The appellant, a former Director General of Police, applied for anticipatory bail after the charge of Section 302 was added. Sessions Judge and High Court denied bail. The Supreme Court considered the appeal, citing the long delay and previous judgments.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Bail Denied

cases.case_name: Sushila Aggarwal and Others v. State (NCT of Delhi) and Another
cases.abstract_facts: The Supreme Court was tasked with deciding on the conditions under which anticipatory bail, as provided under Section 438 of the CrPC, can be granted. In light of conflicting past judgments, the case was referenced to a larger bench to address whether anticipatory bail should be limited to a fixed period and whether it should terminate at the summoning stage or end of trial. The court emphasized the significance of liberty, noting unnecessary arrests and potential for harassment.

cases.case_name: Prem Shankar Prasad v. State of Bihar
cases.abstract_facts: The appellant filed an FIR against the respondent for offences including criminal breach of trust and cheating. The Magistrate issued a warrant, but the respondent absconded, leading to proclamation proceedings. The lower court dismissed the respondent's anticipatory bail application, but the High Court granted it. This appeal challenges the High Court's decision.
cases.disposition: Appeal allowed. High Court's grant of anticipatory bail set aside.
cases.lower_court_outcome: High Court granted anticipatory bail.

cases.case_name: Supreme Bhiwandi Wada Manor Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Maharashtra
cases.petitioner: M/S. SUPREME BHIWANDI WADA MANOR INFRASTRUCTURE PVT. LTD.
cases.abstract_facts: This is a criminal appeal concerning anticipatory bail where the appellant, a company involved in infrastructure projects, accused four of its employees of defrauding it of approximately Rs. 5.08 crores through fabricated documents related to land compensation. The Magistrate ordered an investigation, and the accused were granted anticipatory bail by the Sessions and High Courts. The Supreme Court set aside these bail orders emphasizing the serious nature of the alleged fraud.
cases.disposition: Appeal allowed; anticipatory bail orders set aside
cases.lower_court_outcome: Grant of anticipatory bail to accused by High Court and Sessions Court

cases.case_name: Pratibha Manchanda & Anr. v. State of Haryana & Anr.
cases.abstract_facts: The appellants, alleging ownership of a land parcel in Gurugram, claimed never to have sold it or executed any power of attorney. They discovered that mutations were sought based on a purportedly forged sale deed and power of attorney from 1996. An FIR was lodged against the accused, who sought anticipatory bail from the High Court. The High Court granted bail, but the Supreme Court set aside the bail considering the need for custodial interrogation.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail granted by the High Court.

cases.case_name: BIMLA TIWARI
cases.abstract_facts: The case involves allegations against the respondents of taking money and articles under the pretext of an engagement arrangement for the informant's daughter, which was later called off. The informant accused the respondents of demanding additional money and a vehicle, and failing to return the money after the engagement was canceled. The High Court had granted pre-arrest bail to the accused-respondents, on the condition of payment, which the informant challenged at the Supreme Court.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Pre-arrest bail granted with payment condition.

cases.case_name: X vs State of Rajasthan & Anr.
cases.abstract_facts: The case involves a bail application related to a serious criminal offence. An FIR was lodged by the petitioner against Respondent No. 2 and a co-accused for offences under Section 376D and Section 342 of the IPC. The accused were arrested and a charge-sheet was filed. The High Court granted bail to Respondent No. 2 based on discrepancies between the FIR and the victim's statement under Section 164 CrPC, which led the petitioner to approach the Supreme Court.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Bail granted by High Court

cases.case_name: Shambhu Debnath v. State of Bihar
cases.abstract_facts: The case revolves around an incident where a 20-year-old individual, the nephew of the appellant, was set on fire after being beaten, allegedly by the accused, leading to his death. The accused had been granted anticipatory bail by the High Court despite the serious allegations under section 302 of the IPC. The Supreme Court was approached to review this decision.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail granted by the High Court

cases.case_name: Shambhu Debnath v. The State of Bihar & Ors.
cases.abstract_facts: The case involves the appellant, who saw his nephew on fire, allegedly set ablaze by the accused with an intention to kill. Despite specific allegations and a chargesheet confirming the accusations, the Patna High Court granted anticipatory bail to the accused. The Supreme Court reviewed whether the High Court erred in its decision.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail granted by the Patna High Court.

cases.case_name: Mariam Fasihuddin & Anr. v. State by Adugodi Police Station & Anr.
cases.respondent: State by Adugodi Police Station & Anr.
cases.abstract_facts: The case involves allegations against the appellants of forgery related to obtaining a passport for a minor child. The appellants claim the actions were in line with instructions, but it is alleged that the signatures on the passport application were forged. The case arose amidst personal disputes between the appellants and the respondent husband, leading to competing legal actions.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Trial Magistrate declined discharge; High Court dismissed revision petition.

cases.case_name: Srikant Upadhyay v. State of Bihar
cases.abstract_facts: The appellants filed an application for anticipatory bail connected to FIR No.79 of 2020. This was related to alleged offenses involving assault and accusations of witchcraft under the Indian Penal Code and the Prevention of Witch (Daain) Practices Act. The trial court issued a proclamation under Section 82 Cr.PC after the appellants failed to appear, despite having received summons and warrants. The High Court rejected their anticipatory bail application, leading to this appeal.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail application dismissed by High Court.

cases.case_name: Srikant Upadhyay & Ors. v. State of Bihar & Anr.
cases.abstract_facts: This Supreme Court judgment deals with the denial of anticipatory bail to applicants accused of witchcraft and assault under sections of the Indian Penal Code and the Prevention of Witch (Daain) Practices Act, 1999. The appellants filed for anticipatory bail after non-bailable warrants and a proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. had been issued due to their failure to appear before the trial court despite multiple summonses and bailable warrants. The court examines the propriety of issuing proclamations while an anticipatory bail application is pending.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Application for anticipatory bail dismissed

cases.case_name: Shajan Skaria v. The State of Kerala & Anr.
cases.abstract_facts: The appellant, an editor of an online news channel, published a video on YouTube making derogatory statements against the complainant, a Member of the Kerala Legislative Assembly from a scheduled caste constituency. The video allegedly intended to ridicule the complainant on account of his scheduled caste status. The appellant sought anticipatory bail, which was denied by the Special Judge and the High Court. The Supreme Court had to consider whether a prima facie case was made under Section 3(1)(r) and Section 3(1)(u) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, and whether Section 18 of the Act imposes an absolute bar on anticipatory bail in such cases.
normalized_statutes: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989:3(1)(U)
Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989:3(1)(R)
Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989:18
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail denied by Special Judge and High Court.

cases.case_name: Shajan Skaria v. State of Kerala & Anr.
cases.abstract_facts: The appellant, an editor of an online news channel, published a video on YouTube allegedly making derogatory statements and allegations against the complainant, a Member of the Kerala Legislative Assembly representing a Scheduled Caste reserved constituency. Offences under Section 3(1)(r) and 3(1)(u) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 were alleged. The appellant sought anticipatory bail, which was denied by the Special Judge and the High Court of Kerala, leading to this appeal before the Supreme Court of India.
normalized_statutes: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989:3(1)(U)
Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989:3(1)(R)
Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989:18
cases.lower_court_outcome: Bail application rejected by the Special Judge and affirmed by the High Court.

cases.case_name: Tusharbhai Rajnikantbhai Shah v. Kamal Dayani & Ors.
cases.abstract_facts: The petitioner was apprehended and sought anticipatory bail, after being accused of fraud related to a real estate transaction involving Rs. 1.65 crores. The Supreme Court initially granted him interim protection from arrest. Despite this protection, the petitioner was remanded to police custody, leading to a contempt petition against the remand order.
cases.disposition: Contempt petition listed for next date, SLPs disposed of.
cases.lower_court_outcome: The High Court denied anticipatory bail to the petitioner, which was also refused by the Sessions Court. cases.case_name: Sudeep Chatterjee v. State of Bihar & Anr.
cases.abstract_facts: The case involves a matrimonial dispute between the appellant and his wife, currently in divorce proceedings. The appellant faces charges under Section 498A of IPC and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act. The High Court granted provisional pre-arrest bail with certain onerous conditions, which the appellant challenged in the Supreme Court, arguing they are impractical and violate his rights.
cases.lower_court_outcome: The High Court granted provisional pre-arrest bail with onerous conditions.

cases.case_name: Dhanraj Aswani v. Amar S. Mulchandani & Anr.
cases.abstract_facts: An accused was arrested for involvement in one criminal case. While in custody, he feared an arrest in a different case and applied for anticipatory bail under Section 438 CrPC. The High Court permitted the application, leading to an appeal to the Supreme Court questioning the maintainability of seeking anticipatory bail while already in judicial custody for a separate offence. The Supreme Court affirmed the High Court's view, allowing the anticipatory bail application.
cases.lower_court_outcome: High Court allowed anticipatory bail application

cases.case_name: Devinder Kumar Bansal v. State of Punjab
cases.abstract_facts: The petitioner, an audit inspector, is accused of demanding a bribe in connection with an audit related to development work conducted during his tenure. A co-accused allegedly collected the bribe on his behalf. The petitioner applied for anticipatory bail, which was denied by the High Court. The Supreme Court dismissed the petition for anticipatory bail, emphasizing the gravity of corruption charges and the necessary limitations on liberty to combat corruption.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Bail denied

cases.case_name: Hitesh Umeshbhai Mashru v. The State of Gujarat & Anr.
cases.abstract_facts: This appeal addresses the denial of anticipatory bail by the Gujarat High Court to an appellant facing allegations under Sections 493 and 376(2)(n) of the IPC, for allegedly deceiving the complainant with a false promise of marriage. The parties had a customary, though unregistered, marriage and the appellant later participated in the investigation under arrest protection. With both the investigation's completion and filing of a charge-sheet, the Supreme Court reviewed anticipatory bail granting conditions.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Application for anticipatory bail rejected by Gujarat High Court.

cases.case_name: Ankit Mishra v. State of Madhya Pradesh & Anr.
cases.respondent: The State of Madhya Pradesh & Anr.
cases.abstract_facts: The appellant challenged the High Court's granting of anticipatory bail to the respondent accused of hurling abuses and making death threats. The appellant argued that the respondent has a criminal background, being a habitual offender with multiple FIRs against him. The respondent claimed most past cases resulted in acquittals or bail. The court assessed whether there was a grave error in granting anticipatory bail given these background factors and the nature of offences charged.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail granted to respondent no. 2.

cases.case_name: P. Krishna Mohan Reddy v. State of Andhra Pradesh
cases.abstract_facts: The case involves petitions for anticipatory bail by individuals implicated in a corruption case related to the allocation of liquor orders by the Andhra Pradesh State Beverages Corporation. It is alleged that preferential treatment was given to certain brands, resulting in significant financial transactions described as kickbacks. The petitioners argue political bias and vendetta, while the State presents evidence of financial misconduct. The Supreme Court assesses whether anticipatory bail should be granted, considering the admissibility of co-accused statements under the law.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail denied

cases.case_name: Serious Fraud Investigation Office v. Aditya Sarda
cases.abstract_facts: The case involves an appeal against the anticipatory bail orders granted by the High Court regarding respondents accused of serious economic offences. The Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) initiated criminal proceedings against the respondents for alleged fraudulent activities involving multiple companies. Despite warrants issued for their arrest, the respondents evaded execution, leading to proclamation proceedings. The Supreme Court examined the legitimacy of the High Court's anticipatory bail orders.
cases.disposition: Appeals allowed, orders of the High Court set aside, except in three cases where appeals were dismissed.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail granted by High Court.

cases.case_name: State of Andhra Pradesh v. N. Sanjay
cases.abstract_facts: The respondent, a senior police officer, was accused of misappropriating public funds while serving as Additional Director General of Police, CID, Andhra Pradesh. The allegations involved manipulation of tenders and unauthorized agreements leading to financial irregularities. The High Court granted the respondent anticipatory bail, which was challenged by the State in the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court examined the validity of granting anticipatory bail given the seriousness of the allegations and the necessity for custodial interrogation.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail granted by the High Court of Andhra Pradesh.

cases.case_name: Kiran v. Rajkumar Jivraj Jain & Anr.
cases.abstract_facts: The case involves the denial of anticipatory bail to an accused involved in caste-based violence and hateful utterance. The accused, part of an aggressive group, allegedly assaulted the complainant and his family using derogatory caste language and physical violence, motivated by the complainant's voting action in an election. The High Court initially granted anticipatory bail despite allegations suggesting clear caste-based offences, including threats and assaults in public view, violating the SC/ST Act.

cases.case_name: Anna Waman Bhalerao v. State of Maharashtra
cases.abstract_facts: The case concerns anticipatory bail applications filed by appellants, former government officials, following allegations of facilitating fraudulent property mutations based on forged documents during their tenure. The events occurred between 1996-1998, but the FIR was not filed until 2019. Attempts for anticipatory bail were made at both session and High Court levels, with interim protection granted intermittently. The Supreme Court was approached after the High Court's final rejection of anticipatory bail, amid concerns of inordinate delays in the case.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail applications rejected by High Court.

cases.case_name: Anna Waman Bhalerao v. State of Maharashtra
cases.abstract_facts: The case involves the rejection of anticipatory bail applications filed by former government officials who certified mutation entries on the basis of forged documents, allegedly facilitating illegal property transfer. Although their actions were executed nearly 20 years ago, they were subsequently implicated as accused Nos. 5 and 6. Initially, they were not named in the FIR, and they served in an official capacity with no evidence of personal gain. Despite the extended interim protection, the applications were eventually dismissed due to the gravity of allegations and the necessity of custodial interrogation.
cases.lower_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail applications were rejected by the Sessions Court and later by the High Court.

propositions.quote: no blanket order could be passed under Section 438 Cr.P.C. to prevent the accused from being arrested at all in connection with the case.

propositions.text: The accused must surrender and seek regular bail once the investigation concludes and a chargesheet is filed.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: accused has to surrender to the custody of the Court and pray for regular bail.

propositions.text: The limitations mentioned in Section 437 CrPC cannot be read into Section 438 CrPC when granting anticipatory bail.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: The limitations mentioned in section 437 Cr.P.C. cannot be read into section 438 Cr.P.C.
propositions.verification_note: The anchor text is missing.

propositions.text: An order granting anticipatory bail for a limited duration and thereafter directing the accused to surrender is contrary to legislative intent and judicial principles.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: Order granting anticipatory bail for a limited duration and thereafter directing the accused to surrender is contrary to the legislative intention.
propositions.verification_note: The anchor text is missing.

propositions.text: No inflexible guidelines or straitjacket formula can be provided for the grant or refusal of anticipatory bail, and it should depend on the facts and circumstances of each case.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: No inflexible guidelines or straitjacket formula can be provided for grant or refusal of anticipatory bail.
propositions.verification_note: The anchor text is missing.

propositions.text: The power to grant anticipatory bail is discretionary and should be exercised with caution and based on circumstances.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: The discretion vested with the court under section 438 Cr.P.C. should also be exercised with caution and prudence.
propositions.verification_note: The anchor text is missing.

propositions.text: Repeated applications for bail after absconding and flouting court directions constitute a gross misuse of the process of the court.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: repeated applications are a gross misuse of the process of the court.

propositions.text: No further application for bail, anticipatory or otherwise, will be entertained until a specified sum is deposited as a precondition.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: Deposit of Rupees One Lac
propositions.quote: no further application for bail anticipatory or otherwise will be entertained by any Court until...

propositions.text: The parameters for granting anticipatory bail in serious offenses require satisfaction with certain conditions and recording reasons for the decision.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: Exceptional circumstances
propositions.quote: Parameters for grant of anticipatory bail in a serious offence are required to be satisfied and further while granting such relief, the court must record the reasons.

propositions.text: Anticipatory bail should be granted only in exceptional circumstances where the court finds that the applicant has been falsely implicated and would not misuse his liberty.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: False implication
propositions.quote: Anticipatory bail can be granted only in exceptional circumstances where the court is prima facie of the view that the applicant has falsely been engaged in the crime.

propositions.text: The High Court must not grant anticipatory bail based on mere allegations of a previous dispute and fair antecedents without considering the entire set of parameters and circumstances of the case.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: The High Court erred in not considering the case in correct perspective and allowed the said applications on the grounds that in the FIR some old disputes had been referred to and the accused had fair antecedents.
propositions.verification_note: The anchor text focuses on the court's failure but doesn't explicitly support the proposition's claim.

propositions.text: The nature and gravity of the accusation must be properly comprehended by the court before deciding on anticipatory bail.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: The nature and gravity of the accusation and the exact role of the accused must be properly comprehended before arrest is made.

propositions.text: The Court of Session or the High Court cannot pass an order that allows for the accused to be released on bail upon surrender, as it contravenes statutory provisions.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: The Court of Session or the High Court cannot pass an order that on surrendering [...] shall be released on bail.
propositions.verification_note: The anchor text does not directly support that the Court of Session or High Court cannot pass such orders, it simply discusses the nature of existing judicial orders.

propositions.text: A court cannot issue a blanket order restraining arrest; any interim order must conform to the requirements of Section 438 with suitable conditions imposed.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: The court cannot issue a blanket order restraining arrest and it can only issue an interim order.
propositions.verification_note: The anchor text supports the notion that a blanket order restraining arrest is not permissible and conditions must be imposed.

propositions.text: Passing orders allowing bail upon surrender jeopardizes the interest of the public and individual victims, and curtails regular court powers on bail applications.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: Passing such kind of orders the interest of the collective at large and that of the individual victims is jeopardised.
propositions.verification_note: The anchor text supports the idea that such orders could jeopardize public interest and individual victims as well as curtail regular court powers.

propositions.text: A person declared as a "proclaimed offender" in terms of Section 82 CrPC is not entitled to the relief of anticipatory bail under Section 438 CrPC.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: no question of granting anticipatory bail to a "proclaimed offender".

propositions.text: Section 18 of the SC/ST Act creates a bar for invoking Section 438 CrPC for anticipatory bail in offences under the SC/ST Act.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
normalized_statutes: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act:1989
propositions.quote: Section 18 of the SC/ST Act creates a bar for invoking Section 438 of the Code.
propositions.verification_note: The anchor text does not explicitly create a bar for invoking Section 438 CrPC for anticipatory bail; it only states that the petitioners are not entitled to anticipatory bail.

propositions.text: Courts must verify the averments in the complaint to determine if an offence under Section 3(1) of the SC/ST Act is prima facie made out before deciding on anticipatory bail.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
normalized_statutes: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act:1989
propositions.quote: a duty is cast on the court to verify the averments in the complaint and to find out whether an offence under Section 3(1) of the SC/ST Act has been prima facie made out.

propositions.text: When an offence is registered under the SC/ST Act, courts should not engage in critical analysis of evidence during anticipatory bail proceedings.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: Court is not expected to indulge in critical analysis of the evidence on record.

propositions.text: While granting anticipatory bail, courts must consider the nature and gravity of the accusation, antecedents of the applicant, possibility to flee, and whether the accusation aims to injure or humiliate.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: grant of bail under Section 438(1) of the Code is dependent on the merits and circumstances of a case.
propositions.verification_note: The anchor text does not explicitly support the detailed considerations listed in the proposition.

propositions.text: A condition for anticipatory bail requiring a deposit amount that makes bail impossible is unreasonable and should be set aside.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: The condition should relate to the fairness or propriety of the investigation or trial.
propositions.quote: fixed deposit of Rs. 1,00,00,000/-...is evidently onerous and unreasonable.

propositions.text: Courts must avoid imposing conditions in anticipatory bail that are unrelated to the fairness or propriety of the investigation or trial.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: any condition, which has no reference to the fairness or propriety of the investigation or trial, cannot be countenanced

propositions.text: The words 'any condition' in Section 438(2) of the CrPC permit only reasonable conditions that are pragmatic and do not defeat the order of bail.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: Any condition has to be interpreted as a reasonable condition...and should not defeat the order of grant of bail.
propositions.verification_note: The anchor text indicates conditions can be imposed but doesn't specify they must only be reasonable.

propositions.text: Anticipatory bail under Section 438 of the CrPC is an extraordinary relief and should be granted in exceptional cases where there is apprehension of false implication or no likelihood of liberty misuse.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: the power exercisable under Section 438 of the Code is somewhat extraordinary in character and it is to be exercised only in exceptional cases.
propositions.verification_note: The anchor text supports the idea that anticipatory bail is extraordinary and only granted in exceptional cases, but the term 'extraordinary relief' could imply broader implications than the court's wording.

propositions.text: An absconder or proclaimed offender in terms of Section 82 of the CrPC is not entitled to anticipatory bail.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: when a person...is absconding or concealing himself...he is not entitled to the relief of anticipatory bail.
propositions.verification_note: The anchor text clearly states that absconders are not entitled to anticipatory bail, aligning with the proposition.

propositions.text: Grant of anticipatory bail should not be given without proper analysis and discussion, especially in serious cases.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: All these materials were neither adverted to nor considered by the High Court while granting anticipatory bail.
propositions.verification_note: The anchor text focuses on the consequences of being an absconder and the serious nature of the case, rather than discussing the analysis required for granting anticipatory bail.

propositions.text: The omission of Section 438 CrPC in Uttar Pradesh means there is no concept of anticipatory bail as understood under this section.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: Applicable only in Uttar Pradesh
propositions.quote: There is no concept of "anticipatory bail" as understood in Section 438 of the Code in the State of Uttar Pradesh.
propositions.verification_note: The anchor text clearly states that the omission of Section 438 CrPC in Uttar Pradesh means there is no concept of anticipatory bail as understood under that section.

propositions.text: Despite the omission of Section 438 CrPC, the High Court under Article 226 of the Constitution can still entertain for pre-arrest protection in appropriate and deserving cases.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: Power is to be exercised with extreme caution and sparingly
propositions.quote: The High Court is not bereft of its powers to grant this relief under Art. 226 of the Constitution.
propositions.verification_note: The anchor text supports the proposition that, despite the omission of Section 438 CrPC, the High Court can entertain pre-arrest protection under Article 226.

propositions.text: Article 226 should not be used to circumvent statutory provisions deliberately omitted, like Section 438 in Uttar Pradesh, except in cases of gross miscarriage of justice.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: Must be an exceptional case
propositions.quote: It cannot be resorted to as to back door entry via Art.226.
propositions.verification_note: The anchor text supports the idea that Article 226 should not be used liberally to circumvent the omission of Section 438, except in cases of gross miscarriage of justice.

propositions.text: Police officers must record reasons for making or not making arrests under Sections 41 and 41A CrPC, providing a check against arbitrary arrests.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: Applicable for offences with up to seven years imprisonment
propositions.quote: Amended provisions make it compulsory for the police to record the reasons for making arrest.
propositions.verification_note: The anchor text supports the proposition that police officers must record reasons for making or not making arrests under Sections 41 and 41A CrPC, which provides a check against arbitrary arrests.

propositions.text: The High Court can entertain an application for bail under Section 439 if the accused has surrendered before it, even if the case is committed to Sessions.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: The accused must surrender to the Court.
propositions.quote: There are no restrictions on the High Court to entertain an application for bail provided always the accused is in custody.

propositions.text: Magistrates have limited powers to grant bail in cases involving offences punishable by death or imprisonment for life, unlike the High Court and Sessions Court.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: Only applies to bail under CrPC Sections 437 and 439.
propositions.quote: The regimes regulating the powers of the Magistrate on the one hand and the two superior Courts are decidedly and intentionally not identical.

propositions.text: The terms 'custody', 'detention', and 'arrest' are not synonymous in law, although custody can occur without arrest.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: Applicable for interpreting statutory terms in context.
propositions.quote: The terms 'custody' and 'arrest' are not synonyms even though in every arrest there is a deprivation of liberty is custody but not vice versa.

propositions.text: A person is considered to be in custody for the purposes of Section 439 if they surrender before the court.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: The person must submit to the court's jurisdiction.
propositions.quote: He can be stated to be in judicial custody when he surrenders before the court and submits to its directions.

propositions.text: Anticipatory bail cannot be denied merely because a serious charge such as rape is added after a long period of time, especially when inaction of the prosecutrix contributes to the delay.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: anticipatory bail cannot be denied when such a charge is added after a long period of time and inaction of the prosecutrix is also a contributory factor.

propositions.text: An order for anticipatory bail under Section 438 of the CrPC is intended to provide conditional immunity from arrest, aligning with Article 21 of the Constitution regarding personal liberty.
propositions.speaker: quoted_authority
propositions.quote: anticipatory bail enshrined in Section 438 of the Code is conceptualised under Article 21 of the Constitution

propositions.text: The mere seriousness of a charge like Section 376 IPC should not itself bar anticipatory bail if the circumstances otherwise justify it.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: merely because the accused is charged with a serious offence may not by itself be the reason to refuse the grant of anticipatory bail

propositions.text: The discretion to grant anticipatory bail should be exercised based on a comprehensive evaluation of the case's facts and should not be influenced by the accused's potential to abscond alone.
propositions.speaker: quoted_authority
propositions.quote: The court should also examine the fact whether there is any family dispute between the accused and the complainant

propositions.text: Bail should not be refused as punishment; the purpose is to secure the attendance of the accused at trial.
propositions.speaker: quoted_authority
propositions.quote: the object of bail which is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial, and the proper test to be applied in the solution of the question whether bail should be granted or refused

propositions.text: In cases involving serious allegations of misappropriation of public funds and corruption, anticipatory bail may be cancelled to allow for custodial interrogation if the investigation is being hindered.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: The investigation is impeded by the grant of bail
propositions.quote: the High Court has rightly cancelled the anticipatory bail granted to the appellants.
propositions.verification_note: The proposition is supported but 'favors' should be 'neutral'.

propositions.text: The grant of or refusal of anticipatory bail should depend on the facts and circumstances of each case without strict guidelines.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: No inflexible guidelines or straitjacket formula can be provided for grant or refusal of anticipatory bail.

propositions.text: The court which grants bail also has the power to cancel it, which can be exercised at the instance of various parties if new material or circumstances arise.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: New material or circumstances must be present
propositions.quote: the court which grants the bail also has the power to cancel it.

propositions.text: Discretionary powers in granting anticipatory bail should be exercised judicially, taking into account each case's unique facts.
propositions.speaker: quoted_authority
propositions.quote: courts have to be allowed a little free play in the joints if the conferment of discretionary power is to be meaningful.

propositions.text: High Courts must assign reasons when rejecting anticipatory bail applications under Section 438 CrPC.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: The reasoning must be judicial and specific, not casual or cavalier.
propositions.quote: Single Judge failed to assign any reason for rejecting the bail application.

propositions.text: Bail applications should not be decided in a casual or cavalier manner.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: The High Court must apply judicial mind in its decisions.
propositions.quote: This Court cannot countenance such casual approach of the High Court.

propositions.text: Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, which is available for offences under the IPC, is not applicable in respect of offences under the SC/ST Act, as they fall into a separate and special class related to the practice of untouchability.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: Section 438 of the Code, which is available to an accused in respect of offences under the IPC, is not available in respect of offences under the SC/ST Act.

propositions.text: Section 18 of the SC/ST Act creates a specific bar against invoking Section 438 of the Code for anticipatory bail in cases where a prima facie case under Section 3(1) of the SC/ST Act is made out.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: Section 18 of the SC/ST Act creates a bar for invoking Section 438 of the Code.

propositions.text: The offences under the SC/ST Act are committed to humiliate and subjugate members of Scheduled Castes and Tribes, and such offences cannot be compared to offences under the Penal Code.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: These offences constitute a separate class and cannot be compared with offences under the Penal Code.

propositions.text: Section 37 of the NDPS Act imposes stringent limitations on granting bail for offences involving commercial quantities of contraband.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: These limitations are in addition to those prescribed under the Cr.P.C.

propositions.text: Protection under Section 438 Cr.P.C. is preliminary and does not automatically entitle an accused to regular bail.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: does not mean that he is automatically entitled to regular bail

propositions.text: A coordinate bench's grant of anticipatory bail without considering the stringent requirements under Section 37 of the NDPS Act is incorrect.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: order granting bail to the co-accused was without reference to s. 37 of NDPS Act

propositions.text: Sessions Courts must ensure that interim orders do not mislead into granting regular bail where final orders do not permit.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: did not take note of the final order passed by the High Court

propositions.text: The Supreme Court has the jurisdiction to enforce fundamental rights of life and liberty against any executive or legislative action.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: Undoubtedly, the Supreme Court has jurisdiction to enforce the fundamental rights of life and liberty against any executive or legislative action.

propositions.text: The application of Section 18 of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act cannot bar anticipatory bail if allegations are false or there is no prima facie case.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
normalized_statutes: The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act,:1989
propositions.quote: It cannot be read as being applicable to those who are falsely implicated for extraneous reasons.

propositions.text: The power of arrest must be used judiciously and not as a means of oppression or harassment.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: Arrest brings humiliation, curtails freedom and casts scars forever.

propositions.text: The misuse of Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act can have an adverse impact on societal integration and constitutional values.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
normalized_statutes: The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act,:1989
propositions.quote: Working of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 should not result in perpetuating casteism.

propositions.text: The court can peruse the materials/documents collected during an investigation even before the commencement of trial to satisfy its conscience on several factors, such as the direction of the investigation or consideration of bail.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: It is well-settled that the court can peruse the case diary/materials collected during investigation by the prosecution even before the commencement of the trial.
propositions.verification_note: The proposition is supported by the anchor text regarding the court's ability to peruse investigation materials for bail considerations.

propositions.text: Grant of anticipatory bail is not a right under Article 21 of the Constitution; it is a discretionary relief that must balance individual liberty with societal interests.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: Exceptional circumstances required
propositions.quote: Power under Section 438 Cr.P.C. is an extraordinary power and the same has to be exercised sparingly.
propositions.verification_note: The proposition is supported as the anchor text clearly states that anticipatory bail is discretionary, balancing individual liberty with societal interests.

propositions.text: Economic offences stand as a separate class as they affect the economic fabric of society, warranting stricter considerations in anticipatory bail.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: At the stage of investigation
propositions.quote: Economic offences stand as a class apart.
propositions.verification_note: The proposition is unsupported; the anchor text mentions the need for custodial interrogation but does not address stricter considerations specifically for economic offences.

propositions.text: The court's role is not to monitor investigation processes, and interrogation standards or questioning methods are within the investigating agency's discretion.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: It is not the function of the court to monitor the investigation process.
propositions.verification_note: The proposition is supported by the anchor text stating that monitoring investigation processes is not within the court's role.

propositions.text: The determination of the maintainability of a petition, such as an anticipatory bail application, requires judicial application of mind and cannot be relegated to administrative processes by a court registry.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
normalized_statutes: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act,:1989
propositions.quote: The act of numbering a petition is purely administrative.

propositions.text: The role of the High Court Registry does not extend to deciding the maintainability of petitions based on law, as this is a judicial function that requires determination by a bench.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: The High Court Registry could not have exercised such judicial power to answer the maintainability of the petition.
propositions.verification_note: The proposition claims that the role doesn't extend to deciding maintainability based on law, yet the truth is that it doesn't extend to deciding the maintainability at all.

propositions.text: Long delay in lodging an FIR, like 29 years, can be a valid consideration for granting anticipatory bail.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: Specific facts and circumstances of the case
propositions.quote: a long delay like 29 years as in the present case can certainly be a valid consideration for grant of anticipatory bail.

propositions.text: The status of the appellant, retired Director General of Police, contribution to eligibility for anticipatory bail given the nature of delay and added charges based only on approvers’ statements.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: we are of the opinion that the appellant has made out a case for anticipatory bail.
propositions.verification_note: The statement in the proposition about 'contribution to eligibility' is not found in the anchor text.

propositions.text: The protection granted under Section 438 CrPC should not ordinarily be limited to a fixed period. Conditions under Section 437(3) read with 438(2) should be imposed, but courts may add conditions based on crime severity.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: Peculiar features relevant to the crime
propositions.quote: The protection granted under Section 438 Cr.PC should not always or ordinarily be limited to a fixed period.

propositions.text: The life of an anticipatory bail does not end when the accused is summoned or charges are framed, but can continue till end of trial unless circumstances necessitate otherwise.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: Special or peculiar features
propositions.quote: The life of an anticipatory bail does not end generally at the time and stage when the accused is summoned.

propositions.text: Anticipatory bail once granted can extend till the end of trial unless limited by conditions or circumstances warranting otherwise.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: Court discretion based on circumstances
propositions.quote: The life or duration of an anticipatory bail order does not end normally.
propositions.verification_note: The proposition states anticipatory bail lasts till the end of trial unless limited. However, the anchor text suggests the imposition of conditions could limit it.

propositions.text: An anticipatory bail order should not be blanket, granting protection from arrest for unspecified offences. It should be confined to the incident for which arrest is apprehended.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: Specific to incident
propositions.quote: An order of anticipatory bail should not be “blanket”.
propositions.verification_note: The proposition states bail should be confined to specific incidents, which is supported. However, 'favors' is incorrect as it favors the prosecution.

propositions.text: An accused who is declared as an absconder under section 82 CrPC is generally not entitled to anticipatory bail.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: Thus the High court has committed an error in granting anticipatory bail to respondent No.2 – accused ignoring the proceedings under Section 82-83 of Cr.PC.
propositions.verification_note: The proposition is accurately supported by the anchor text.

propositions.text: When granting anticipatory bail, the court should seriously consider the initiation of proclamation proceedings under sections 82-83 CrPC and not ignore them.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: The aforesaid relevant aspect on grant of anticipatory bail ought not to have been ignored by the High Court.
propositions.verification_note: The proposition is accurately supported by the anchor text.

propositions.text: The nature of the accusation, rather than the fact that it arises out of a business transaction, should guide the decision on granting anticipatory bail.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: What is required to be considered is the nature of allegation and the accusation and not that the nature of accusation is arising out of a business transaction.
propositions.verification_note: The proposition is accurately supported by the anchor text.

propositions.text: Anticipatory bail may not be granted when serious allegations of fraudulent misappropriation are involved, especially when detailed in an FIR.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: Seriousness of allegations
propositions.quote: Having regard to the seriousness of the allegations no case for anticipatory bail was made out.
propositions.verification_note: The anchor text does not support the claim regarding anticipatory bail and serious allegations.

propositions.text: The validity of a Magistrate's order under Section 156(3) of the CrPC, if not challenged, cannot be questioned by the High Court while considering anticipatory bail applications.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: The Magistrate’s order under Section 156(3) was not under challenge before the High Court and has attained finality.
propositions.verification_note: The anchor text does not provide sufficient support for the proposition.

propositions.text: An investigation under Section 156(3) of the CrPC ordered by a Magistrate happens before taking cognizance and need not involve examining the complainant on oath under Section 200.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: The Magistrate orders investigation under Section 156(3) it would be a different kind of investigation.
propositions.verification_note: The anchor text does not substantiate the proposition regarding investigations under Section 156(3).

propositions.text: Anticipatory bail is designed to safeguard individual rights and prevent harassment from arrest, while balancing against public interest and ensuring the gravity of the offence is considered.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: The relief of Anticipatory Bail is aimed at safeguarding individual rights.

propositions.text: The custody of suspects is justified to ensure fair and thorough investigation when there are allegations of forgery and misappropriation of property.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: custodial interrogation...is, therefore, imperative to unearth the truth.

propositions.text: The original GPA's absence raises doubts about the legitimacy of transactions claimed by the accused and underscores the need for investigation.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: Absence of GPA
propositions.quote: The 1996 GPA has not yet seen the light of the day.

propositions.text: In cases of alleged land fraud, thorough investigation by authorities is necessary, and anticipatory bail complicates uncovering the truth.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: prima facie evidence to indicate that...should be viewed with scepticism.

propositions.text: Bail cancellation should occur only with substantial reasons, but correcting an erroneous bail order differs.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: Erroneous bail order
propositions.quote: setting aside an erroneous bail order is altogether different from cancelling bail.

propositions.text: Granting bail should not be contingent on repayment or offers of repayment, as it is independent of criminal law processes.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: the process of criminal law cannot be utilised for arm-twisting and money recovery, particularly while opposing the prayer for bail

propositions.text: Repayment or offers of payment should not automatically lead to granting or denial of pre-arrest or regular bail.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: in a given case, the concession of pre-arrest bail or regular bail could be declined even if the accused has made payment

propositions.text: Recovery of money is within the realm of civil proceedings, not criminal law, particularly in the context of bail.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: Recovery of money is essentially within the realm of civil proceedings.

propositions.text: In serious offences like rape, once the trial commences and prosecution begins examining witnesses, courts should typically avoid granting bail.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
conditions: except on undue delay of trial through no fault of the accused
propositions.quote: Ordinarily in serious offences like rape, once the trial commences and the prosecution starts examining its witnesses, the Court...should be loath in entertaining the bail application of the accused.
propositions.verification_note: The anchor text supports the proposition but 'favors' does not align with the intent of the proposition being in favor of the prosecution.

propositions.text: Courts should not grant bail by scrutinising discrepancies in the victim's statement and FIR once the trial has commenced.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: The moment the High Court exercises its discretion...by looking into the deposition of the victim, it will have its own impact on the pending trial.
propositions.verification_note: The anchor text supports the proposition but 'favors' does not align with the intent of the proposition being in favor of the prosecution.

propositions.text: If an accused on bail resides in the same village as the victim, conditions should be imposed to prevent contact or influence over the witness or victim.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court
propositions.quote: ...without disturbing the order of bail passed by the High Court, we direct that the Respondent No.2 – herein shall not enter the said village till the completion of the trial.
propositions.verification_note: The anchor text supports the proposition but 'favors' does not align with the intent of the proposition being in favor of the prosecution.

propositions.text: Courts must generally consider the nature and gravity of the offenses, the role attributed to the applicant, and the facts of the case when deciding whether to grant anticipatory bail.
propositions.speaker: quoted_authority
